messages:
alex: FYI support ticket from AcmeFin: sudden spike in latency and ~5% 403s starting ~08:12 UTC. They say requests are being routed to eu-west while their app is pinned to us-west-2. Can we triage? :warning:
sara: on it. do we have traces or routing decisions? any healthcheck logs?
alex: attaching snippets from support logs (redacted):
```
[08:11:58] route-decider: probe(us-west-2/edge-04) -> FAIL (connect ECONNREFUSED) ttl_expiry=30000
[08:11:58] route-decider: mark unhealthy us-west-2/edge-pool for 30s (suppression=ttl)
[08:11:59] routing: fallback -> eu-west-1, session-id=... latency_inc=180ms
[08:12:03] auth: token-issuer mismatch for region eu-west-1 -> 403 client_id=acmefin-prod
```
Note: the probe target was 10.2.4.12:8081 per config. Customer expects 8080.
priya: hmm config drift? the health probe port mismatch will produce false negatives and trigger failover. did the probe service recently change default port?
sara: checking gitops history for health-probe-config in us-west-2. give me 2 mins.
ryan: tagging routing svc owners @priya, @sara. This also caused a billing bump since traffic crossed region. Customer is asking for root cause and mitigation.
emma-cust: (from customer) "We didn't change anything on our end. Our config points at 8080. Why is Redwood calling 8081?"
priya: found a merge yesterday that updated probe image. It introduced a default override of port->8081 when a missing annotation exists. Some clusters lacked the annotation -> probe fell back to 8081.
sara: that would explain the false negative. two-part mitigation: 1) quick rollback of the probe image to v1.4.2 on us-west pools; 2) short-term bump of healthcheck grace to avoid immediate suppression.
alex: can we run a quick patch command? customer is sensitive to latency, want minimal disruption.
priya: propose: `kubectl -n redwood rollout undo ds/probe-daemonset --to-revision=3` on us-west-2 edge nodes; and `routingctl set-suppression --region us-west-2 --ttl 8s` (was 30s).
sara: before changing ttl, we should repro locally: curl internal probe endpoint with both ports to show 8080 responds and 8081 fails.
ryan: repro steps for support to show customer:
1) `curl -sS -D - http://10.2.4.12:8080/health` -> 200 OK
2) `curl -sS -D - http://10.2.4.12:8081/health` -> connection refused
3) request trace that shows `X-Region: us-west-2` original header then `routed-to: eu-west-1` in routing headers

alex: posted above to ticket. also note: 403s were caused by issuer mismatch because the JWT issuer for eu-west routes differs (regional key). once routed cross-region, token validation fails -> 403. include this in RCA.
priya: I'm going to start the rollout undo now. ping when done.
incident-bot: Deploy event: rollback of probe-daemonset (namespace=redwood, cluster=us-west-2) started by priya at 08:25 UTC — tracking #deploy-4521
sara: after rollback, I'm going to run a few synthetic checks and watch routing decisions for 10 minutes.
priya: rollback succeeded on 6/6 nodes.
sara: initial synthetic run: probes now show healthy on us-west edge pool, routing decisions switched back to us-west-2, latency normalizing.
ryan: customer notified with explanation and timeline. they asked for permanent fix (guardrail for probe port annotation).
alex: next steps for postmortem: 1) add validation to gitops pipeline to reject probe config that omits port annotation; 2) add canary check to ensure probe-default-change doesn't auto-apply to prod pools; 3) consider making suppression backoff adaptive (avoid single-probe port mismatch causing full region failover).
emma-cust: thanks for the quick response team. please keep me posted on the postmortem.
priya: filing PR with validation and a small patch to default behavior. assigning to @ryan for review.
alex: closing incident thread once postmortem PRs are merged and customer confirmed. great job everyone :thumbsup:
